sentences.en: As the presidential race moves into high gear, abortion is at the center of it.
sentences.zh: 随着总统竞选进入白热化，堕胎问题已成为核心议题。

sentences.en: Republican-controlled states continue to impose new bans, including just this week in Florida.
sentences.zh: 共和党控制的州继续实施新的禁令，包括本周刚在佛罗里达州实施的禁令。

sentences.en: But in Washington, the Biden administration is fighting back, challenging one of those bans in a case that is now before the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 但在华盛顿，拜登政府正在进行反击，在目前提交给最高法院的一起案件中挑战其中一项禁令。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues Pam Bellick and Abby Van Sickle explain.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事帕姆·贝利克和艾比·范·西克尔将对此进行解读。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, May 1St.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月1日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Pam, in the two years since Roe v.
sentences.zh: 那么帕姆，在罗诉韦德案被推翻后的两年里，

sentences.en: Wade was overturned, more than a dozen states have instituted pretty strict bans.
sentences.zh: 十几个州已经实施了相当严格的禁令。

sentences.en: But as all of these bans are happening at the state level, something is happening at the federal level.
sentences.zh: 但正如所有这些禁令都在州一级发生一样，联邦一级也在发生一些事情。

sentences.en: And that is the Biden administration is fighting back in a kind of unusual way.
sentences.zh: 那就是拜登政府正在以一种不同寻常的方式进行反击。

sentences.en: And that effort came to the Supreme Court last week.
sentences.zh: 而这一努力上周提交到了最高法院。

sentences.en: Tell me about it.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the case that went before the Supreme Court last week is basically a fight between
sentences.zh: 好的，上周提交给最高法院的案件基本上是

sentences.en: the state of Idaho and the Biden administration over whether Idaho's abortion ban violates a federal law that's been on the books for decades.
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州与拜登政府之间的一场争论，焦点在于爱达荷州的堕胎禁令是否违反了一项已存在数十年的联邦法律。

sentences.en: And if it does, then does Idaho have to change its abortion ban?
sentences.zh: 如果违反了，那么爱达荷州是否必须修改其堕胎禁令？

sentences.en: And this case really gets at a bigger question about whether there are still ways that the federal government can limit states' ability to ban or restrict abortion.
sentences.zh: 这个案件真正触及了一个更大的问题，即联邦政府是否还有办法限制各州禁止或限制堕胎的能力。

sentences.en: Okay, just to clarify here, the Supreme Court, of course, in Dobbs, left it to states to determine their own abortion policies.
sentences.zh: 好的，澄清一下，最高法院当然在多布斯案中将堕胎政策的决定权留给了各州。

sentences.en: But what role was left for the federal government?
sentences.zh: 但联邦政府还剩下什么角色呢？

sentences.en: Was there one?
sentences.zh: 还有吗？

sentences.en: Well, Dobbs eliminated the constitutional right to abortion, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，多布斯案取消了宪法规定的堕胎权，对吧？

sentences.en: It said that there's no guarantee anywhere in the country that people have a right to abortion access and that states can make their own laws around abortion.
sentences.zh: 它表示全国任何地方都没有堕胎权的保证，各州可以制定自己的堕胎法律。

sentences.en: But it didn't completely eliminate any other way that federal government laws or regulations interact with abortion.
sentences.zh: 但它并没有完全消除联邦政府法律或法规与堕胎相互作用的其他任何方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that left the Biden administration looking around to try to figure out what, if anything, the federal government could do to weigh in on abortion.
sentences.zh: 所以这让拜登政府四处寻找，试图弄清楚联邦政府如果能做些什么来干预堕胎问题。

sentences.en: And it turned out that there were really very few tools left to the federal government.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，联邦政府剩下的工具确实非常少。

sentences.en: But it does find this one federal law from 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 但它确实找到了这项40年前的联邦法律。

sentences.en: And the law really has nothing to do with abortion.
sentences.zh: 而这项法律实际上与堕胎毫无关系。

sentences.en: It doesn't mention abortion.
sentences.zh: 它没有提到堕胎。

sentences.en: It is all about emergency room medical care.
sentences.zh: 它完全是关于急诊室医疗护理的。

sentences.en: But the Biden administration thinks that it has found a way to use this law to fight some of the strictest abortion bans that states like Idaho are putting into play.
sentences.zh: 但拜登政府认为，它已经找到了一种方法，利用这项法律来对抗像爱达荷州这样正在实施的最严格的堕胎禁令。

sentences.en: So in other words, the Biden administration is basically rummaging around in its back closet
sentences.zh: 换句话说，拜登政府基本上是在其后壁橱里翻箱倒柜，

sentences.en: looking for some way to protect abortion rights in there doesn't find much, but it does find this old dress.
sentences.zh: 寻找保护堕胎权的方法，虽然没找到多少，但确实找到了这件旧衣服。

sentences.en: And that's the law that's in front of the Supreme Court right now that you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 而这就是你所说的目前在最高法院审理的那项法律。

sentences.en: Tell me about that law.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说那项法律吧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this is the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act.
sentences.zh: 这就是《紧急医疗和劳动法》。

sentences.en: As an abbreviation, it's referred to as EMTALA.
sentences.zh: 缩写为EMTALA。

sentences.en: And EMTALA was passed to try to fix a problem that was getting increasingly widespread in the country in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: EMTALA的通过是为了试图解决一个在20世纪80年代全国范围内日益普遍的问题。

sentences.en: And what was happening was a problem called patient dumping.
sentences.zh: 当时发生的问题被称为“病人倾倒”。

sentences.en: What this meant was that mostly private hospitals, if a patient showed up to their emergency room
sentences.zh: 这意味着主要是私立医院，如果病人出现在他们的急诊室，

sentences.en: and the patient didn't have insurance or couldn't otherwise pay, these private hospitals were closing their doors to these patients.
sentences.zh: 而病人没有保险或无法支付费用，这些私立医院就会对这些病人关上大门。

sentences.en: And they were sending them to public hospitals, county hospitals.
sentences.zh: 他们把病人送到公立医院，即县立医院。

sentences.en: And there were these horrific examples of people who were showing up in emergency rooms at public hospitals, having been kicked out of the private hospital with stab wounds and
sentences.zh: 有一些令人震惊的例子，人们带着刀伤和

sentences.en: gunshot wounds.
sentences.zh: 枪伤被私立医院赶出来，出现在公立医院的急诊室。

sentences.en: I mean, there was one case in Texas where a man with third degree burns stumbled into a
sentences.zh: 我是说，德克萨斯州曾发生过一起案件，一名三度烧伤的男子跌跌撞撞地走进

sentences.en: county hospital with a catheter and an IV line that had been inserted by the private hospital that had kicked him out.
sentences.zh: 一家县立医院，身上还插着私立医院赶他出来时插入的导尿管和静脉输液管。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And this was creating a lot of public alarm and getting a lot of attention.
sentences.zh: 这引起了公众的极大恐慌，并受到了广泛关注。

sentences.en: And some of the cases involved pregnant women in labor.
sentences.zh: 其中一些病例涉及临产的孕妇。

sentences.en: And these private hospitals were turning them away before their babies could be born.
sentences.zh: 这些私立医院在她们的孩子出生前就把她们拒之门外。

sentences.en: And one example, in Texas, this woman went to a private hospital.
sentences.zh: 在德克萨斯州的一个例子中，一名妇女去了私立医院。

sentences.en: And when she told them that her husband had just lost his job, they pushed her legs together, started an IV line, and sent her over to this county hospital.
sentences.zh: 当她告诉他们丈夫刚失业时，他们强行合上她的双腿，挂上静脉输液，把她送到了这家县立医院。

sentences.en: And she was crowning, according to the doctor who was at the hospital.
sentences.zh: 据当时在医院的医生说，她当时已经快生了。

sentences.en: And the baby was just coming any minute she delivered in the hallway of the hospital.
sentences.zh: 孩子随时都会出来，她在医院走廊里就把孩子生下来了。

sentences.en: So this is a serious public problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个严重的公共问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Congress is under pressure to take action to try to prevent this.
sentences.zh: 国会面临采取行动防止这种情况的压力。

sentences.en: And so in 1986, they enact EMTALA, this federal law, which really was landmark.
sentences.zh: 因此在1986年，他们颁布了EMTALA，这项联邦法律确实具有里程碑意义。

sentences.en: It was really kind of groundbreaking.
sentences.zh: 它确实具有开创性。

sentences.en: And basically what this law does is it says emergency rooms in hospitals that receive Medicare
sentences.zh: 这项法律基本上规定，接受医疗保险资助的医院的急诊室，

sentences.en: funding, which is almost all hospitals in the country, have to treat any patient that shows up with any emergency medical condition.
sentences.zh: 也就是全国几乎所有的医院，都必须治疗任何出现紧急医疗状况的病人。

sentences.en: It requires emergency rooms to stabilize the patient.
sentences.zh: 它要求急诊室稳定病人的病情。

sentences.en: They have to give at least a basic standard of treatment to make sure that their health doesn't get worse, that their condition doesn't deteriorate.
sentences.zh: 他们必须提供至少基本的治疗标准，以确保病人的健康不会恶化，病情不会加重。

sentences.en: And if they can't do that, they don't have the ability to do that.
sentences.zh: 如果他们做不到，没有能力做到，

sentences.en: They have to transfer the patient to a hospital that can.
sentences.zh: 他们必须将病人转院到有能力的医院。

sentences.en: And it crucially does not matter if they can't pay for it or if they have no insurance.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，病人是否付得起钱或是否有保险并不重要。

sentences.en: But where does abortion come into this?
sentences.zh: 但堕胎在其中扮演什么角色呢？

sentences.en: I mean, we're obviously talking about this in the context of the abortion fight, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们显然是在堕胎斗争的背景下讨论这个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: From what you're saying, it sounds like the law really had more to do with women coming in to try to have their babies delivered, not women coming in to try to have abortions.
sentences.zh: 从你所说的来看，听起来这项法律更多是关于妇女进来分娩，而不是妇女进来堕胎。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, abortion is not mentioned in EMTALA.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，EMTALA中没有提到堕胎。

sentences.en: And it was not really something that even came up in the passage of the law.
sentences.zh: 而且在法律通过时，这甚至不是一个被提及的问题。

sentences.en: The law was really addressing these horror stories of women in labor being turned away from hospital emergency rooMs.
sentences.zh: 该法律真正解决的是临产妇女被医院急诊室拒之门外的恐怖故事。

sentences.en: But the law does include this two-word phrase that decades later becomes part of the abortion debate.
sentences.zh: 但该法律确实包含了一个双词短语，几十年后成为了堕胎辩论的一部分。

sentences.en: And that phrase is unborn child.
sentences.zh: 那个短语是“未出生的孩子”。

sentences.en: Now, at the time, that phrase shows up very much in this context that we've been talking about of women who are about to deliver a baby.
sentences.zh: 当时，这个短语出现的背景正是我们一直在讨论的即将分娩的妇女的情况。

sentences.en: So abortion is not mentioned in this law at all.
sentences.zh: 所以这项法律根本没有提到堕胎。

sentences.en: And it wasn't even really in the background of at the time when it was passed.
sentences.zh: 而且在通过时，它甚至不在背景中。

sentences.en: After EMTALA is passed, it has been used over the last four decades to basically try to ensure
sentences.zh: EMTALA通过后，在过去的四十年里，它基本上被用来确保

sentences.en: that patients with all kinds of conditions don't get turned away from emergency rooMs.
sentences.zh: 各种病情的病人不会被急诊室拒之门外。

sentences.en: And it doesn't come into the abortion debate until nearly four decades later when the Biden administration decides that it can use this law to try to at least open some cracks into
sentences.zh: 直到近四十年后，当拜登政府决定利用这项法律试图至少在这些非常僵化的州堕胎禁令中打开一些裂缝时，它才进入堕胎辩论。

sentences.en: these very rigid state abortion bans.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 所以你把我们带回了我们开始这次谈话的起点，也就是当前的这个案件，对吧？

sentences.en: So you brought us back to the beginning where we started this conversation, which is this current case, right?
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州诉拜登政府案。

sentences.en: Idaho versus the Biden administration.
sentences.zh: 那么这场争斗究竟是如何爆发的呢？

sentences.en: So how did that fight actually break out?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 在罗诉韦德案被推翻后，包括爱达荷州在内的许多州实施了近乎全面的堕胎禁令。

sentences.en: So after Roe v.
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州的禁令对堕胎有非常有限的例外情况。

sentences.en: Wade was overturned, a number of states, including Idaho, put into place near total abortion bans.
sentences.zh: 唯一允许堕胎的情况之一是为了防止孕妇死亡。

sentences.en: Idaho's ban has very limited exceptions for abortion.
sentences.zh: 但拜登政府发布了一份备忘录，上面写着，嘿，医院，嘿，各州，我们只是提醒你们，EMTALA的解释适用于来到急诊室并需要紧急堕胎的妇女。

sentences.en: And one of the only times abortion is allowed is to keep a pregnant woman from dying.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登政府的意思是，这项联邦法律规定，防止死亡并不是急诊室必须治疗病人的唯一原因。

sentences.en: But the Biden administration issues a memo and it says, hey, hospitals, hey, states, we're
sentences.zh: 他们还必须防止人们的健康状况恶化，因为有许多情况是妇女正在严重出血或患有严重感染，但可能并没有生命危险。

sentences.en: just reminding you the interpretation of EMTALA applies to women who come to emergency rooms and need emergency abortions.
sentences.zh: 因此，孕妇可能需要堕胎来挽救生命的情况与她可能需要堕胎来保护健康的情况之间存在巨大的鸿沟。

sentences.en: So what the Biden administration is saying is this federal law says preventing death is not the only reason that emergency rooms have to treat people.
sentences.zh: 所以拜登政府说，看，这项联邦法律要求你不仅要保护妇女的生命，还要保护妇女的健康，这当然使它与爱达荷州的禁令直接冲突，对吧？

sentences.en: They also have to prevent people's health situation from getting worse because there are
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: many situations where a woman is bleeding severely or she has a severe infection, but maybe she's not about to die.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府在这里追求的是更广泛的东西，超越了急诊室护理的东西。

sentences.en: And so there's a pretty wide gulf between situations where a pregnant woman might need an abortion to save her life and when she might need an abortion to protect her health.
sentences.zh: 他们在这里针对的是爱达荷州禁令中的一个概念，即除了挽救母亲生命外，你不能进行干预。

sentences.en: So the Biden administration is saying, look, this federal law requires that you protect not just the woman's life, but also the woman's health, which, of course, brings it into
sentences.zh: 通过指出EMTALA并说这项法律要求你进行干预以保护病人的健康，他们想迫使有这些严格禁令的州承认并允许在许多此类怀孕并发症病例中进行堕胎。

sentences.en: direct conflict with Idaho's ban, right?
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，它确实也想在这些堕胎禁令的基础中制造一道裂缝。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And what the Biden administration is going after here is something much broader, something that goes beyond emergency room care.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你所说的基础上的裂缝。

sentences.en: What they're targeting here is the concept in Idaho's ban that you can't intervene except to save the life of the mother.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是关于处于这种情况的妇女这一狭窄群体，而是从法律上给了他们潜在的途径去做更大的事情。

sentences.en: And by pointing to EMTALA and saying this law requires you to intervene to protect a patient's
sentences.zh: 拜登政府实际上决定对这项EMTALA法律采取非常积极的态度。

sentences.en: health, they want to force states with these strict bans to acknowledge and allow abortions in a number of these cases of pregnancy complications that happen.
sentences.zh: 因此，在罗诉韦德案被推翻后不久，拜登政府起诉了爱达荷州，称你们的堕胎禁令违反了这项联邦法律，你们的堕胎禁令不能成立。

sentences.en: And by doing that, it really wants to also create a crack in the foundation of these abortion bans.
sentences.zh: 帕姆，爱达荷州对此有何回应？

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 它在这里的论点是什么？

sentences.en: So that's the crack in the foundation that you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州表示它没有违反EMTALA。

sentences.en: It's not just about this narrow demographic of women who would be in this situation, but it gives them legally, potentially, a path to do something bigger.
sentences.zh: 它指责拜登政府想把急诊室变成堕胎诊所，并想强迫爱达荷州的医生违反爱达荷州的法律提供堕胎服务。

sentences.en: And the Biden administration actually decides to be very aggressive with this EMTALA law.
sentences.zh: 这也是“未出生的孩子”这个短语出现的地方。

sentences.en: And so very soon after Roe v.
sentences.zh: 爱达荷州正在利用EMTALA中的那种措辞。

sentences.en: Wade is overturned, the Biden administration sues Idaho and says, your abortion ban is violating this federal law and your abortion ban cannot stand.
sentences.zh: 它说，因为联邦法律提到了“未出生的孩子”，这意味着当孕妇去急诊室时，你有两个病人需要考虑。

sentences.en: And Pam, what does Idaho say in response?
sentences.zh: 如果你在做堕胎手术，那么在他们看来，你就是在杀死这两个病人中的一个。

sentences.en: What's its argument here?
sentences.zh: 这就是他们取缔这种能力的原因。

sentences.en: So Idaho says it is not violating EMTALA.
